issues.failure_explanation: The definition of f_D uses the scalar arc-length measure |dξ| in the Cauchy-type term, while the proof that Re f_D = D (and the jump formula) uses the complex differential dξ. With |dξ|, the real part is an arc-length-weighted integral of Re(1/(2πi)(ζ−η1)), not the normal-derivative kernel of D.

failure_location.quote: In fact, $\Re  f_\mathcal{D}[\phi] = \mathcal{D}[\phi]$, which is a function on $\mathbb T_\tau\backslash\partial\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |dξ| by dξ in the first integral of the complex double-layer definition, or redefine f_D to match the Cauchy-type integral used in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The analytic complex double-layer potential used to identify nullspaces and prove injectivity is not the object established in the proof; dependent nullspace and Dirichlet-bijection arguments are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Complex double-layer definition uses |dξ| where the proof and identity require dξ
issues.why_classification: This is a local definition/proof mismatch with a forced one-symbol repair; the intended theory and all substantive results can survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Since z−z̄ = 2i Im z, (z−z̄)^2 = −4(Im z)^2. Thus Re f_G = −(1/2π)log|θ1| − (Im z)^2/(2b), not the stated Green's function G, which has + (Im z)^2/(2b). The calculation drops the factor i.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the sign in f_G to −(z−z̄)^2/(8b) (or equivalently correct the displayed calculation) so that Re f_G = G.
issues.overall_effect: Item (3) of the lemma is false; the claimed complex Green's function representation does not reproduce G. Other cited items of the lemma are not directly affected.
issues.title: Sign error in the real-part representation of the torus Green's function
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local sign fix to a standalone representation; it does not alter the main layer-potential architecture or the results that cite the other items.

issues.failure_explanation: In the Nyström construction, D_{(l,i),(k,j)} = h^k_j ∂ν_ξ G(z^l_i−z^k_j), while D_s,(l,i),(k,j) = h^k_j ∂ν_z G(z^l_i−z^k_j). The transpose would be (D^T)_{(l,i),(k,j)} = h^l_i ∂ν_ξ G(z^k_j−z^l_i), which differs by quadrature weights and by the non-symmetric kernel/normal dependence in general.

failure_location.quote: Note that \( D_s = D^T \), where $D$ is defined in Appendix~\ref{s: dirichlet num implementation}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove or correct the statement D_s = D^T and use the explicitly defined D_s entries (or construct the true weighted adjoint matrix) in the implementation description.
issues.overall_effect: The stated matrix construction for the Neumann BVP solver, and any Steklov solver that reuses D_s via this transpose claim, is unreliable if the transpose relationship is used.
issues.title: Neumann discrete matrix incorrectly stated as the transpose of the Dirichlet matrix
issues.why_classification: The explicit D_s definition is already present and is the correct object; the repair is a local correction to a false matrix relationship, not a change to the underlying theory.

issues.failure_explanation: The continuous Steklov BIE uses S0[φ] = S[(I−M)φ] + φ̄. The discrete eigenproblem as written uses only S(I−M)φ, so it is invariant under adding a constant to φ. The subsequent reconstruction u = φ̄ + S(I−M)φ is not invariant. Without fixing the constant component of φ (or including the φ̄ term in the eigenproblem), the algorithm does not guarantee that the reconstructed u satisfies ∂ν u = σ u. The definition of M also mixes a scalar/row-vector average with a matrix projection.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the discrete mean projection consistent and fix the gauge: either impose φ̄=0 (take φ=(I−M)φ and output S[(I−M)φ]) or replace the right-hand side by the discrete S0, S(I−M)φ + φ̄ 1, matching Theorem thm: steklov.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical Steklov EVP implementation and its eigenfunction reconstruction/residual claims are unsupported as written; the projected density eigenvalues may be relevant, but the stated output u_k is ambiguous.
issues.title: Discrete Steklov formulation omits the S0 constant term / gauge fixing
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local gauge/projection correction in the numerical section; a comparable corrected algorithm is supported by the source and the theoretical results and advertised method can survive.
